clue.text: Spotted Mass working at a clue

parts.note: M is a standard abbreviation for Mass, as in the church service or the physics quantity

indicators.note: working here means set in motion and reworked, so the letters of at a clue get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at Mass is caught puzzling over a crossword clue instead of praying.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass looks like the church service, but it only supplies its abbreviation; 'working' is the anagram signal, shuffling the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Maculate is a rare literary word for stained or blemished, the opposite of immaculate.

parts.note: modes are ways or manners of doing something

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so the last letter of the word saint is taken

explanation.surface: A saint is held up as the model of humble living.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone unassuming who does not boast of their merits.

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is an island in the Greek Dodecanese
a coterie is a select set or clique of people

explanation.surface: A clique on a Greek island holiday spoil themselves rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper or spoil someone is to treat them with excessive indulgence.

clue.text: Makeshift structure with skimpy unfinished roof

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Makeshift structure with skimpy unfinished roof (4-2)': skimpy gives LEAN, but no reading of 'unfinished roof' gives TO; probably an OCR misreading (e.g. of 'top') that neither search nor a scan confirms.
annotationWithheld.clue: Makeshift structure with skimpy unfinished roof

clue.text: Pottery, note, a tractor churned up

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: churned up describes soil turned over by the tractor, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A tractor ploughing a field turns up buried pottery shards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churned up' suits a tractor ploughing, which hides that it is the anagram signal; the note is the sol-fa syllable, placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is unglazed brownish-red fired clay, used for pots and figurines.

indicators.note: in places the fastening word inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS is the standard prefix abbreviation for a steamship
to tack is to fasten or secure something with tacks

explanation.surface: A crewman fixes down the funnels aboard a steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacks are the tall chimneys on a ship or factory that carry away smoke.

clue.text: Hot, beginning to refresh in current

indicators.note: in puts that single letter inside the word for current

parts.note: topical matters are current, of present interest

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of the word refresh is used

explanation.surface: In the heat you start to feel refreshed by a cool current of air or water.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the world's hottest regions, so tropical weather is sweltering.

indicators.note: slicing means cutting into, so the male letter goes between the two other pieces

parts.note: co- is a prefix meaning joint or together, as in co-owner
homely in the British sense means plain, simple and unpretentious

explanation.surface: A man carving a joint of beef at a homely Sunday lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Beef is a verb here, slang for grumble; the joint and slicing suggest a Sunday roast, but joint is the prefix CO.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is slang for to grumble or moan about something.

indicators.note: in places the road abbreviation within the rearranged letters
a road recobbled has its stones relaid, so the letters of Saxony are rearranged

explanation.surface: Workers relay a stone road somewhere in Saxony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recobbled' turns SAXONY into SA-ONYX, and 'in' puts RD into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonyx is a gemstone, a variety of onyx with layers of sard.

clue.text: One run in various spades, then loses heart

indicators.note: in sets the two letters inside the rearranged spades
various signals that the letters of spades come in a different arrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
R is the abbreviation for run, as on a cricket scoresheet

explanation.surface: A card player holding a run of spades gives up hope of winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' turns SPADES into DESPAS, and 'in' puts I and R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope, which is what losing heart means.

indicators.note: attendant on means accompanying, so the order word goes along beside the royal letters

parts.note: form can mean order or arrangement, as in a set form of proceedings
Her Majesty, the late Queen, was Elizabeth Regina, ER

explanation.surface: A courtier waits upon Her Majesty under an old court order.
explanation.definitionFit: Former means belonging to an earlier time, as in a former president.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Pimpernel's origin (8)': too short for any wordplay giving SPECTRAL; likely cut short in OCR, and a search of the text found no fuller version.

clue.text: Old square retreat back in part of Venice

indicators.note: back means the whole sequence is read in reverse order

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so T can stand for square
a lair is a den, an animal's retreat

explanation.surface: A tourist retreats back to an old square in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses O + T + LAIR as a whole to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the old commercial district of Venice, famous for its bridge.

clue.text: Electronic device possibly producing echo in Prom?

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: At a Proms concert, feedback echoes round the hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are the BBC's summer concert season at the Royal Albert Hall; 'possibly' shuffles ECHO IN PROM.
explanation.definitionFit: A mic is an electronic device turning sound into an electrical signal.

clue.text: Workers organisation is adroitly dealt with

indicators.note: dealt with suggests cards being dealt out, so the letters are redistributed

explanation.surface: A union's affairs are handled skilfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidarity was the Polish independent trade union led by Lech Walesa in the 1980s.

clue.text: Less disposed to confine jobbing writer in chains

indicators.note: to confine means to enclose, so the writer goes inside the rearranged letters
disposed means arranged, so the letters of less are set out another way

parts.note: a hack is a writer who churns out work to order

explanation.surface: A reluctant author is locked up in chains.
explanation.walkthrough: Less disposed looks like 'less willing', but 'disposed' rearranges LESS to S-LES, holding HACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Shackles are metal fetters linked by a chain to restrain a prisoner.

clue.text: Suggestion of one who needs a hand?

definitions.text: Suggestion of one who needs a hand?

parts.words: Suggestion of one who needs a hand?
parts.note: a suitor asking for a hand in marriage makes this kind of suggestion, not someone needing help

explanation.walkthrough: A hand here is a hand in marriage, not help with a task.
explanation.definitionFit: A suggestion or plan put forward, and also an offer of marriage.

clue.text: Supplement habit, but not with cocaine

indicators.note: not with means the cocaine letter is removed

parts.note: a habit, in drug slang, is an addiction
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A drug habit is kicked once cocaine is left out.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition is something added on, a supplement to what was there.

indicators.note: unravelled means untangled, so the letters are taken apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A family historian untangles the Hardy family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereditary things are passed down from ancestors.

indicators.note: hooks means catches hold of, so the beer surrounds the teetotal letters

parts.note: beer is a drink
a sobersides is a serious sober person; TT stands for teetotal

explanation.surface: A pint of beer tempts even a teetotaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of higher quality than another.

clue.text: Fancy one time going around Spain?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: going around means the time word encircles the letter for Spain

parts.note: a date is a particular time
E is the international vehicle registration code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: One fancies taking a trip around Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as a verb means imagine, and to ideate is to form an idea of something.

indicators.note: an introduction is the start, so only the opening letter of wedding is used

parts.note: rites are formal ceremonies

explanation.surface: Someone writes the opening words for a wedding service.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose a letter, song or poem is to write it.

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: a rich flavour is full-bodied

explanation.surface: A drinking vessel that is not quite filled to the brim.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupric means containing copper, a metal, in a chemical sense.

clue.text: Agricultural apparatus produced by Spanish academic

parts.note: Sp is the standard abbreviation for Spanish
a reader is a senior university lecturer in Britain, just below professor

explanation.surface: A Spanish lecturer turns out to have invented a farm machine.
explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a Reader is an academic rank just below professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A spreader is a farm machine that scatters fertiliser or manure across fields.

definitions.meaning: a lass or girl, especially in Scotland and northern England
a famous collie in Eric Knight's novel and the films

explanation.surface: A female creature appears in a storybook.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish word for a girl, and also the name of the heroic collie dog of novel and screen.

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
It is the short form of Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: An Italian artist leaves a painting behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painted or photographic likeness of a person.

indicators.note: burgeoning suggests growing and changing, so the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: A country lane bursts into leaf in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring is a water source, not the season; 'burgeoning' shuffles LANE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a saline is a salt spring or salt lake.

indicators.note: into places the mistake word inside the rows

parts.note: tiers are ranks or rows, one above another
to err is to slip up or make a mistake

explanation.surface: Soldiers make a mistake and fall in among the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: Terriers is British slang for Territorial Army volunteers, part-time soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force, are nicknamed Terriers.
